I read the target method and the full QA test file. The tests all call `LiteralStringVar.create(...)` with strings that either contain encoded Reflex var tags or are plain strings created recursively inside the method.

From the method body:

- Line 1184 always runs first to normalize `_var_type`.
- If the input string contains `REFLEX_VAR_OPENING_TAG`, line 1186 enters the parsing branch.
- Inside that branch, the loop at 1191 searches for encoded tags, 1192 gets the span, 1194 appends the literal prefix, 1196 extracts the serialized id, and 1198–1204 resolve global immutable vars and trim `value`.
- The numeric-id condition spans 1198–1200; for both positive and negative serialized ids, line 1199 is reached when the left side of the `or` is false and the negative-number check must be evaluated.
- After each match, 1206 updates `offset`; when no more matches exist, 1208 is the failed-search check and 1210 builds the final list with the trailing string.
- 1211 is executed as part of the list comprehension body for filtering empties, but nested listcomp events are excluded by the question, so only the outer method’s own line events count. The outer method still has line 1211 as part of evaluating the comprehension statement, and that line is within the exact function body shown.
- The tests with mixed literals and vars all produce more than one filtered element, so 1213 runs and the single-element return block at 1214–1218 is not taken.
- Then 1220–1226 compute `literal_strings` and compare lengths. Because every tagged test includes at least one non-literal `Var`, the all-literal recursive-join return at 1227–1241 is not taken. Still, 1220, 1221, 1223, and 1226 are executed while evaluating that condition.
- The mixed cases then fall through to 1243–1245 to build `ConcatVarOperation`, and 1248–1251 return it, either directly or converted to `StringVar`.
- Test nine passes `_var_type=StringVar`, so line 1251 is covered; the other mixed-tag tests with default `_var_type` cover 1249–1250 and return directly.
- The recursive calls that create plain literal segments like `"hello "`, `"!"`, `"/page/"`, etc. do not enter the tag branch, so they cover the plain-string return at 1254–1258.
- Those recursive plain-string calls still execute 1184 and 1186 before skipping the `if`.
